text:
elaine: Quick heads-up — next Wednesday (2065610000) we're shipping a small behavioral change to the SDKs that affects passthrough of unknown request params. This is NOT a full deprecation, it's a compatibility tightening behind a rollout flag. TL;DR: new default will STRICTLY validate top-level params and reject unknown ones; we will gate the change under feature flag `legacy_param_passthrough` for 30 days before flipping it for new installs. Docs + migration guide live now: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/param-gating

matt: Thanks — important for some customers. Two quick q's: 1) Is this for all SDKs (py/js/go)? 2) How will this show up in errors?

elaine: 1) Yes — py/js/go will all receive the same behavior. 2) You'll get a 400 with a short error message listing the unknown keys, e.g. `Unknown parameter: fooBar`. We'll also include a remediation hint in the body and a link to the migration snippet.

jordan: Can we have a code snippet showing the compatibility flag usage? Also, will Dedicated/Private customers be auto-upgraded?

elaine: Snippet below (py and js). Dedicated/Private: we won't flip for on-prem/private by default — ops teams get the flag and can flip when ready. Hosted customers: new workspaces created after the grace-period will have strict validation; existing workspaces will be held behind the flag for 30 days and we'll send email + console banners before flipping.

elaine: Python snippet:

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'], feature_flags={"legacy_param_passthrough": True})
# keep legacy behavior while you update callers
resp = client.generate(text="hi", unknown_param="x")
```

elaine: JavaScript snippet:

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, featureFlags: { legacy_param_passthrough: true } })
// legacy behavior retained until you remove unknown params
await client.generate({ text: 'hi', unknownParam: 'x' })
```

sara: Nice. For docs, can we add an automated lint rule in the lang-agnostic examples to surface unknown param usage? Might help customers find call sites.

elaine: Agreed — @docs-bot will add a checklist item to the docs PR and we plan to auto-run a quick grep/lint on examples.

docs-bot: Created task #DOCS-487: add param-lint + example updates. PR incoming.

matt: Timeline? What should engineering and SEs tell customers today?

elaine: Timeline: announce now (this thread + email), docs + migration guide live now, feature-flag rollout to all workspaces in 7 days for testing, 30 day opt-in hold for existing workspaces, flip for hosted new workspaces after 30 days. We'll send two reminder emails and console banner at 14 and 3 days left. Tell customers: small stricter validation is coming, use the `legacy_param_passthrough` flag to buy time, update callers to remove unknown params (we'll provide a script).

jordan: Will we provide a compatibility-check script for repos?

elaine: Yes — small CLI that scans code for common param names and patterns + runs smoke calls against a staging workspace. Plan to publish as `redwood-sdk-compat-check` in our examples repo.

matt: Will release notes include sample diffs?

elaine: Yes — release notes will have before/after request shapes and example error responses. We'll also add an automated example re-run in CI to catch broken snippets.

deploy-bot: docs-site: publish succeeded — https://docs.redwood.dev/sdk/param-gating (build #5421)

matt: acked. I'll add a one-pager for CSMs with customer tiers that might need extra support.

elaine: Thanks everyone — if you have migration-edge cases, drop them in this thread and we'll expand the guide. :sparkles:
